question: Should OpenClaw adopt this public plugin-SDK and Gateway-protocol contract for external verification approvals as the permanent core extension seam, or should the contract be narrowed before merge?
rationale: The PR adds new durable plugin APIs, protocol methods, native projections, user-facing approval actions, and persisted state; tests cannot decide whether that is the intended long-term product boundary.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow host-owned contract
options.body: Confirm the Gateway-owned lifecycle, verifier capability, and reusable-grant API as the intended stable extension seam, then require upgrade and successful verifier proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the public surface
options.body: Keep the host-owned approval design but reduce or redesign the SDK, protocol, or persisted grant surface before accepting it as a supported contract.

options.title: Defer core adoption
options.body: Keep the tracker open and pursue the verifier as an external integration until a maintainer sponsors a core API contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrow host-owned contract
recommendation.body: Confirm the Gateway-owned lifecycle, verifier capability, and reusable-grant API as the intended stable extension seam, then require upgrade and successful verifier proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked tracker identifies Kevin as the person who accepted the design RFC that this PR implements.
